 By Ian Mitchelmore BBC Sport Wales ,  At Racecourse Ground, Wrexham Lewis O'Brien cancelled out Adam Armstrong's opener as Wrexham held in-form Wolverhampton Wanderers to a draw at the Racecourse Ground. 
 Armstrong's sumptuous volley put the visitors ahead midway through the first half.
 But O'Brien levelled with a header - his first goal of the season - just two minutes later to earn Phil Parkinson's side a point.
 The draw brought an end to Wolves' three-game winning run, although Cesar Peixoto's side - who sit third ahead of the later weekend fixtures - extended their unbeaten sequence to six matches.
 The Red Dragons, albeit potentially only briefly, rose to 15th having extended their unbeaten home run to three games.
 What did you make of Wrexham's display? 
 Send us your views on Wolves' display 
 Image source, Alex Dodd/Shutterstock Image caption, Wolves are winless in their four away league games against Wrexham
 Callum Doyle and Armstrong both had efforts on target early on in what was a fairly low-key opening to the contest in north Wales.
 Rob Mac was delayed in linking up with fellow Wrexham co-owner Ryan Reynolds at the Racecourse Ground, although, upon his arrival, the game exploded into life after Mateus Mane was well denied by Anthony Patterson.
 Moments after that chance, Nasser Djiga's long ball upfield caught out the Wrexham defence, and Armstrong smartly volleyed beyond Patterson to open the scoring with his fifth goal of the campaign.
 Wolves briefly went to the top of the live league table, although the joy of the away supporters was short-lived.
 Issa Kabore's lofted cross from the right found O'Brien who nodded beyond Jose Sa from six yards out - the midfielder's first goal since January.
 O'Brien and Ollie Rathbone both had efforts either side of Marshall Munetsi's wayward shot as the contest remained finely poised.
 Peixoto's side lifted the tempo after the restart as Mane drilled into the side netting before Fer Lopez blazed over the crossbar moments later.
 The hosts spurned a glorious chance to go ahead after the hour mark as Jacques Ekomie's free kick fell to Kieffer Moore who failed to guide his effort on target.
 Patterson made further saves to deny Lopez and Tommy Doyle as the visitors looked the likelier to net a late winner.
 But Wrexham proved a tough nut to crack as the Welsh side earned a point to ensure they go into the international break in positive spirits - with Wolves still firmly in the mix for a top two spot.
